WOODS RUN DIGEST

Friday edition

November 20, 2026

U.S. — FOREST PRODUCTS / NOVEMBER 18 LEGISLATION

House bill seeks stronger markets for underused wood

Representatives Kim Schrier and GT Thompson introduced the Forest Bioeconomy Act, H.R. 11072, on November 18 to connect Forest Service research more closely with manufacturers and develop uses for wood that has little commercial value. The proposal links forest-management material with product development and mass-timber research.

Schrier’s summary describes a small-business voucher program for access to Forest Service research facilities and an Office of Technology Transfer. These are proposed tools, with no application window open. The House measure has been referred to committees and follows S. 2598, introduced in July 2025. It has not become law; lower housing costs and stronger wood demand remain sponsors’ objectives.

Schrier: proposal and sponsor summary → · Congressional Record: introduction and referral → · Senate companion text →

By the Numbers

Latest available observations as of 2026-11-20. Dates and comparison periods vary by series; monthly figures remain unchanged between releases.

IndicatorLatestChange
U.S. on-highway dieselEIA U.S. on-highway diesel; taxes includedUS$5.94/galWeek of November 16, 2026; released November 17−US$0.19/gal
−3.1%Versus November 9: US$6.13/gal
Lumber futuresJanuary 2027 lumber futures (CME LBRF27)US$533.00/MBFNovember 19, 2026 settlementUnavailableNovember 12 January settlement not independently verified
Madison’s lumber indexMadison’s weekly lumber indexUS$444.00/MBFWeek ending November 13, 2026−US$5.00/MBF
−1.1% (calculated)Versus week ending November 6: US$449.00/MBF
Hardwood lumber PPIBLS WPU0812; 1982=100; not seasonally adjusted284.3 index pointsOctober 2026; released November 13−1.3 points
−0.4%Versus revised September 2026: 285.6
U.S. single-family housing startsCensus U.S. single-family starts; annualized estimate864,000 units (SAAR)October 2026; released November 18+33,000 units (SAAR)
+4.0%Versus revised September 2026: 831,000
Canadian dollarBank of Canada; Canadian dollars per U.S. dollarC$1.43 per US$1.00Daily average, November 19, 2026−C$0.00 per US$1.00
−0.1%Versus November 18: C$1.43 per US$1.00

Housing starts are annualized estimates, not actual monthly units, and are subject to revision. The hardwood PPI is an index, not a dollar price. Exchange rates are daily averages. MBF means thousand board feet. The October single-family starts monthly change has a published ±9.0-percentage-point 90.0% confidence interval and is not statistically significant. The named January settlement is from the contract table, which differs from continuous-series historical prices. The November 12 same-contract settlement could not be independently confirmed. Display rounding follows the approved format. Changes are calculated from unrounded observations, so rounded currency levels may look unchanged even when a small movement occurred.

Sources:
EIA U.S. on-highway diesel; taxes included
Investing.com January contract settlement
CME delivery calendar
Madison’s November 13 index
BLS hardwood lumber PPI via FRED
Census U.S. single-family starts; annualized estimate
Bank of Canada daily averages

Trade Policy Watch

U.S. Commerce’s November 19 notice corrects a calculation error in the 2024 Canadian softwood-lumber subsidy review. Resolute’s rate falls from 12.42% to 12.35%; the reviewed non-selected companies’ rate falls from 14.11% to 14.08%. West Fraser’s 15.31% is unchanged. The notice sets amended cash-deposit requirements for covered entries from October 19. These are countervailing-duty rates, not the combined burden of all lumber duties; producer/exporter combinations and the appendix determine applicability. Commerce: corrected rates and deposit instructions

Wood Products & Markets

CANADA — BIOMASS MARKETS / NOVEMBER 19 ANNOUNCEMENT

Canada opens a purchasing route for wood-based carbon removal

Canada’s Treasury Board announced 19 competitively established carbon-removal standing offers on November 19. Designated federal departments, agencies and Crown corporations can use them through March 31, 2029, with an extension option.

Wood-related entries include the Pessamit Innu First Nation’s Quebec forest-biomass storage and wildfire-risk project, Ontario’s Green Ventures biochar project and Quebec’s Carbonity biochar plant. The new purchasing route offers a potential demand signal for biomass-based removals. Standing offers do not establish purchase volumes, payments to these suppliers or feedstock contracts, and they are not an open grant or landowner-enrollment program.

Treasury Board: purchasing framework and named projects →

Action Detector

CANADA — ALBERTA / SEASONAL FIELD GUIDANCE

Calgary winter-burning guidance calls for checks below the surface

Alberta’s November 18 Calgary Forest Area bulletin says recent snow lowered wildfire danger, but some winter burning projects may still lack suitable conditions. Its guidance calls for at least 15 centimetres of snow cover where winter burns are conducted, with weather and fire-spread potential assessed before ignition.

The bulletin directs continuous monitoring, smoke-warning signs and complete extinguishment before leaving a burn unattended. Piles can retain heat below the surface and reignite days or weeks later. This is regional seasonal guidance for crews managing woody debris, rather than a new universal burning rule.

Calgary Forest Area: current winter-burning guidance →

Under the Radar

CANADA — ONTARIO / HARDWOOD MILL RECOVERY

Five-log study connects purchasing decisions with mill recovery

A November 11 National Hardwood Lumber Association account describes a yield study at Haliburton Forest and Wildlife Reserve in Ontario. Inspectors tested five logs spanning grades and diameters to compare what the mill recovered from different raw material. Those observations offer a mill-specific diagnostic, not an industry benchmark.

The association connects lumber volume and grade with handling costs, processing expenses and the equipment time a log occupies. Its account identifies controllable cuts at the headsaw’s opening face, edger and trimmer. The study concerns recovery and purchasing decisions at an existing operation; no expansion or independently verified savings are announced.

National Hardwood Lumber Association: Haliburton yield study →

BARK — Bick’s App for Resource Know-How

BARK is a browser-based field-calculator app for tree and stand measurements. Its tools cover timber volume, biomass, basal area, sampling dimensions and related estimates, with formulas and references shown.

CANADA — ONTARIO / HARDWOOD MILL RECOVERY

Five-log study connects purchasing decisions with mill recovery

A November 11 National Hardwood Lumber Association account describes a yield study at Haliburton Forest and Wildlife Reserve in Ontario. Inspectors tested five logs spanning grades and diameters to compare what the mill recovered from different raw material. Those observations offer a mill-specific diagnostic, not an industry benchmark.

The association connects lumber volume and grade with handling costs, processing expenses and the equipment time a log occupies. Its account identifies controllable cuts at the headsaw’s opening face, edger and trimmer. The study concerns recovery and purchasing decisions at an existing operation; no expansion or independently verified savings are announced.
